source.title_or_context: **Table 6** Core components of cardiac rehabilitation in cardiac transplantation.

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Exact review confirms extensive assessment, exercise, diet, weight, lipid, blood-pressure, tobacco, and psychosocial instructions for cardiac-transplant rehabilitation. Medication recommendations, descriptive outcome/mechanism claims, and explicit evidence-gap cells coexist with non-drug instructions, so the table is mixed and requires adjudication.

entities.surface_form: an unusually low BP, a change of HR, unexplained weight gain or fatigue
personal hygiene and general measures to reduce the risk of infection

normative_assertions.notes: The patient-assessment table lists these clinical and imaging assessments.
Exercise-capacity testing is specified four weeks after surgery.
The source states that rapid appropriate treatment is necessary for acute rejection.
Patients are to practise self-monitoring for possible early rejection signs.
The source directs education on hygiene and infection-risk-reduction measures, followed by the concrete precautions.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Clinical: wound healings • Chest X-ray: pleural effusion and diaphragmatic paralysis • Echocardiography: pericardial effusion • Exercise capacity: cardiopulmonary exercise stress test four weeks after surgery to guide detailed exercise recommendations. For testing protocols, small increments of 10W per min on bi-cycle ergometer, or modified Bruce protocols or Naughton protocols on treadmill are appropriate; ramp protocols for treadmill • Physician knowledge of the anatomical and physiological reasons for limited exercise tolerance: e.g. the immune-suppression therapy side effect (impairments of inflammatory response, metabolism, osteoporosis, steroid-associated myopathy or polyneuropathy) • Risk of acute rejection: rapid, appropriate treatment is necessary. Patients should be instructed to practise self-monitoring: an unusually low BP, a change of HR, unexplained weight gain or fatigue may be early signs of rejection even in the absence of major symptoms • Patients and physiotherapists should be educated to adhere to the recommendations concerning personal hygiene and general measures to reduce the risk of infection: • Good dental hygiene, no toothbrush older than four weeks • Frequent hand washing using liquid soap • Avoidance of close contact with people with infectious diseases (measles, chickenpox, mumps, mononucleosis, common cold, flu) • Avoidance of contact with persons having received oral polio vaccination for eight weeks • If indispensable, pets in the household only under strict precautions and with limited contact with patient • No gardening without gloves • No contact with decaying plants, fruits, vegetables • No stay near construction work and compost heaps • No mould inside the home • Hydroculture (hydroponics) better than potting compost in the home • Avoidance of swimming in public baths

factual_relations.notes: The source explicitly says the exercises prevent immunosuppressive-therapy side effects.
The source states that exercise intensity relies more on perceived exertion than on a specific HR.

normative_assertions.notes: Respiratory frequency and the speech rule are identified as intensity-control measures.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Chronic dynamic and resistance exercises prevents the side-effects of immunosuppressive therapy • Exercise intensity relies more on perceived exertion than on a specific HR (due to denervation of the heart). The respiratory frequency is also important to control intensity, by using the 'speech rule' (see Table 1)

entities.surface_form: active and systematic mobilization of the upper and lower limbs
the second or third week after transplant
combined resistance exercise (muscle strength) and aerobic training (walking)

normative_assertions.notes: Respiratory training and mobilization are advised before discharge.
Aerobic exercise may start in the second or third post-transplant week.
Aerobic exercise is to stop during corticosteroid bolus therapy for rejection.
Resistance exercise is to be added after 6–8 weeks.
The regimen specifies at least 30–40 minutes per day; intensity continues in the next source part.

text_units.verbatim_text: • Before hospital discharge, respiratory training, active and systematic mobilization of the upper and lower limbs are advisable • After discharge, aerobic exercise may be started in the second or third week after transplant but should be discontinued during corticosteroid bolus therapy for rejection. Resistance exercise should be added after 6–8 weeks • Regimen: at least 30–40 min/day of combined resistance exercise (muscle strength) and aerobic training (walking) at moderate

entities.surface_form: 2–3 sets with 10–12 repetitions per set at 40–70% 1-RM, with a full recovery period >1 min between each set
five sets of 10 repetitions at 70% of 1-RM
low intensity ( VO_{2peak} < 50\% or 10% below anaerobic threshold) or peak work load (<50%)
sets of short- or long-lasting exertion periods (30 s to 4 min) at high intensity (> 85% VO_{2max} ), followed by short- or long-lasting recovery periods (30 s to 4 min)

normative_assertions.notes: This fragment continues the regimen from the preceding source part.
The source specifies resistance-training set, repetition, intensity, recovery, and goal parameters.
Aerobic training should begin at the stated low-intensity criteria and then increase progressively.
The source defines HIIT exertion/recovery intervals and intensity.

text_units.verbatim_text: level, slowly progressing warm-up, closed-chain resistive activities (e.g. bridging, half-squats, toe raises, use of therapeutic bands) and walking/Nordic walking/cycling Resistance training: 2–3 sets with 10–12 repetitions per set at 40–70% 1-RM, with a full recovery period >1 min between each set. The goal is to be able to do five sets of 10 repetitions at 70% of 1-RM Aerobic training should start at low intensity ( VO_{2peak} < 50\% or 10% below anaerobic threshold) or peak work load (<50%) and progressively increase HIIT: sets of short- or long-lasting exertion periods (30 s to 4 min) at high intensity (> 85% VO_{2max} ), followed by short- or long-lasting recovery periods (30 s to 4 min). 79

entities.surface_form: Raw meat Raw seafood Unpasteurized milk Cheese from unpasteurized milk Mouldy cheese Raw eggs Soft ice Grapefruits, pomelo, ginger, turmeric

factual_relations.notes: The parenthetical explicitly states effects of the listed items on calcineurin-inhibitor concentrations through CYP3A4.

normative_assertions.notes: The source lists foods to avoid for dietary infection prophylaxis.

text_units.verbatim_text: Dietary infection prophylaxis – food to be avoided: Raw meat Raw seafood Unpasteurized milk Cheese from unpasteurized milk Mouldy cheese Raw eggs Soft ice Grapefruits, pomelo, ginger, turmeric (effects on calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, cyclosporine) concentrations through CYP3A4)

normative_assertions.notes: The source notes reasons to follow the diet but explicitly states that controlled studies for CAV or survival have not been published.

text_units.verbatim_text: There are good reasons to follow a Mediterranean style diet, even though controlled studies in these patients to assess the influence of nutrition on CAV or survival have not been published

factual_relations.notes: The source states that obesity increases cardiac-allograft-vasculopathy risk.

normative_assertions.notes: Avoidance of overweight is explicitly mandatory.
Daily exercise and a healthy diet are recommended to control obesity.

text_units.verbatim_text: Avoidance of overweight is mandatory to balance the side-effects of immunosuppressants, to limit the classical cardiovascular risk factors Obesity increases the risk of cardiac allograft vasculopathy. It should be controlled by daily exercise and healthy diet

factual_relations.notes: Hyperlipidaemia is stated to increase CAV risk.

normative_assertions.notes: The source recommends statins, daily exercise, and healthy diet to control hyperlipidaemia; the mixed target types are preserved.
Ezetimibe may be added to statins under concentration control.

text_units.verbatim_text: Hyperlipidaemia increases the risk of CAV. It should be controlled by statins, daily exercise and healthy diet Statins (pravastatin, fluvastatin) not only lowered LDL-C levels but also decreased the incidence of CAV and significantly improved survival. Ezetimibe are the second line therapy and can be added to statins under the immunosuppression concentrations control

factual_relations.notes: The source attributes the dose-related adverse effects to interaction with cyclosporine.
Dose-related myopathy and myolysis are associated with statin therapy in this statement.

normative_assertions.notes: The adverse effects and cyclosporine interaction must be considered.

text_units.verbatim_text: Statins are now part of standard therapy, but dose-related myopathy and myolysis because of interaction with cyclosporine must be considered

factual_relations.notes: Hypertension is explicitly linked to immunosuppressive therapy.
Hypertension is explicitly linked to denervation of cardiac volume receptors.
The source states that hypertension is sensitive to a low-sodium diet.
Nifedipine and diltiazem may increase calcineurin-inhibitor effects due to drug interactions.

normative_assertions.notes: The fragment states a target value but contains no explicit act in this sentence.
Amlodipine and ACEIs/ARBs are identified as first-choice treatment.
Diuretics usually complete the treatment regimen.
Beta-blockers are contraindicated during the early term.
The statement describes beneficial later treatment use; retained as a condition-dependent source-style instruction with human review.
source_trigger_texts: showed the beneficial effects as a treatment

text_units.verbatim_text: Target BP is 130/80 mmHg Hypertension is linked to immunosuppressive therapy and denervation of cardiac volume receptors It is sensitive to a low-sodium diet. Treatment with amlodipine and ACEIs/ARBs are first choice, usually completed by diuretics. Beta-blockers are contra-indicated as they hamper the already delayed chronotropic response of the denervated heart during the early term but they showed the beneficial effects as a treatment more than 1–1.5 years after HTX and in the case of post-transplant heart failure development. Nifedipine and diltiazem may increase the effects of calcineurin inhibitors due to the drug interactions

normative_assertions.notes: Smoking cessation is a prerequisite for transplantation in most centres.
Psychological support may be needed to prevent resumption of smoking.

text_units.verbatim_text: Cessation of smoking is a prerequisite for transplantation in most centres. Psychological support may be needed so patient does not resume smoking post-transplantation

entities.surface_form: Clear medical information and advice on life after transplant
patient guilt or problems with high levels of anxiety and apprehensiveness

normative_assertions.notes: Information and advice are stated as needed to manage the listed psychosocial challenges.
Recommendations must be presented carefully while preserving patient choice and offering support.

text_units.verbatim_text: Clear medical information and advice on life after transplant are needed to manage challenges such as patient guilt or problems with high levels of anxiety and apprehensiveness Careful presentation of recommendations is necessary, leaving the choice up to the patient and offering every possible support he/she may need to adjust
